shapes.label: IdeaMesh   Cooker · Mesh · Integration
shapes.desc: Top bar with the app name, the three page tabs (Mesh is selected) and a link to the ideas repo on the right. The tabs are how you move between pages, and the browser back button works too.

shapes.label: Describe today's idea…
shapes.desc: The prompt that starts a run. Free text. Enter runs the mesh, and Shift+Enter adds a new line.

shapes.label: Open in Cooker
shapes.desc: Takes the prompt to the Cooker page to refine it with chat, design questions and a sketch before it runs. This replaces the zoom-in window from the first sketch.

shapes.label: Run mesh
shapes.desc: Sends the prompt through every green or yellow brick whose checks have passed, and pushes the results. It is disabled while the prompt is empty. During a run it turns into 'Stop run', which finishes the current brick and then stops.

shapes.label: Brick network
shapes.desc: Canvas of bricks and their connections, from left to right. Each brick has a coloured ring: red and blurred means sketched, yellow means prototype, green means live. While a run is in progress, the active brick pulses and the arrows fill in as each step finishes. Drag the background to pan.

shapes.label: −   Fit   +
shapes.desc: Zoom controls grouped together: zoom out, fit everything in view, and zoom in. Ctrl+scroll also zooms.

shapes.label: Prompt
shapes.desc: Start node for the prompt. Clicking it puts focus in #2.

shapes.label: PassRotor
shapes.desc: Yellow ring (prototype). It supplies credentials to the repo brick, shown by the arrow down to #9.

shapes.label: Ideas repo
shapes.desc: Green ring (live). Writes the dated idea folder and README, then commits and pushes. Shows the last push time. Clicking it selects it in #14.

shapes.label: Portfolio + text
shapes.desc: Yellow ring. Adds the idea to the portfolio and generates its text from the README. Its '!' icon in the top-right corner means it failed in the last run, and hovering or focusing the icon shows the error and when it happened.

shapes.label: Website · local folder
shapes.desc: Yellow ring. Copies the idea page into a local website folder instead of a public site for now.

shapes.label: Weekly recap
shapes.desc: Example of a sketched brick: red ring and blurred, and not connected. It is skipped in runs until its sketch is approved on the Cooker page. Clicking it opens it in #14.

shapes.label: Add brick
shapes.desc: Opens a list of bricks to add, including ideas from the repo. A new brick is placed on the canvas. To connect it, you pick 'Takes from' in #16 with the keyboard or drag from its edge.

shapes.label: Inspector
shapes.desc: Details of the selected brick. With nothing selected it says 'Select a brick to see its checks and settings.'

shapes.label: Portfolio + text · v2
shapes.desc: Name, version and ring colour of the brick, with an on/off switch. Off means the brick is skipped in runs; this is different from sketched.

shapes.label: Checks · Takes · Gives · Settings
shapes.desc: First the check layers and whether each is passed (Sketch approved now; Contract, Dry run and Manual OK later). Then what the brick takes from and gives to, and its editable settings, such as the tone of the generated text. A warning appears here when a connection's output doesn't match the next brick's input.

shapes.label: Open in Cooker
shapes.desc: Opens this brick on the Cooker page to change it or review its sketch.

shapes.label: Upgrade to v3
shapes.desc: Swaps in the newer version and keeps its connections. It is only shown when an upgrade exists, and an 'Undo upgrade' link stays in the run log until the next run.

shapes.label: Run log
shapes.desc: Latest runs, newest first: the idea name, one dot per brick (passed, failed, skipped), and links to the commit, the portfolio entry and the local web page. Clicking a failed dot reruns just that brick. When there are no runs yet it says 'No runs yet. Type an idea above and press Run mesh.'

note: Mesh page: the prompt and run controls on top, the brick network with ring colours in the middle, the inspector with check layers on the right, and a taller run log at the bottom. Check that the ring colours and the '!' icon read clearly.
